body:
# Audit: mass-parametrized fiber birth, Sections1–4

Source: `candidate 8b9ef51c1503d49a`.

Result: PASS after one preliminary-path sentence was corrected by the author. The exact descent response, sign, and new-candidate controls require no repair. This audit does not certify universal availability of the geometric birth or favorable capture law, and does not audit Section5's separate triangle classification.

The geometric hypotheses explicitly prescribe the COMPLETE actual sampled fibers. A convex hull is not substituted for that hypothesis. An exposed new sampled base has a pure-base cap isolating its own O(epsilon) mass, so its candidates cannot compete with a positive old maximum. The alternative lattice-global cap-group criterion is also correct: the positive weighted continuous normals cancel, and at any integer base at least one group has nonnegative averaged margin. Its caps cover the entire continuous fiber plane. Moving a containing cap parallel through a candidate only lowers its outward-smoothed mass at fixed continuous normal. Individual cap budgets, rather than their weighted average alone, are correctly required for this direct cover.

The covariance numerator of a born fiber x_q+epsilon^(1/d)D_q is epsilon^(1+2/d)|D_q|Cov(D_q), because covariance is centered at that fiber's own centroid. Thus the old within-fiber numerator is unchanged to first order and the new denominator M+epsilon gives Sigma'=-Sigma/M. Consequently Gamma'=-Gamma/(2M). At Gamma=1, q' =q/(2M), so the old cap contribution has derivative A/(2M), with A=int q psi(q) dmu<=0. The sign in the source is correct.

Scaling the new fibers back to fixed D_q proves their mass contribution is epsilon int Psi(q)dnu+o(epsilon). The Lipschitz error is O(epsilon^(1+1/d)/h) for fixed h>0. The finite source-menu envelope therefore has the displayed response int W_i dnu+Abar_i/(2M)-beta after normalization. The old coarea balance sum theta_ij S_ij u_ij=0 is the correct mark-gradient cancellation. The source explicitly retains the finite-envelope regularity assumptions and a separate argument controlling all new candidates; the covariance calculation alone is not used as a substitute.

For ordinary depth h=0, strict birth margins make each small fiber wholly captured or wholly missed uniformly under O(epsilon) source motion. Without strict margins the limiting contribution can depend on the born shape and the source displacement, so the separate qualification is necessary and correctly stated.

The original preliminary-path wording claimed that an exposed vertex of the SAMPLED base hull could not enter the real projection of a Minkowski path before its final time. That claim was unnecessarily strong and false. For example in n=2,d=1 let

    C_old=conv( { (z1,0,0):-2/5<=z1<=-1/10 }
                union { (z1,1,x):0<=z1<=1, |x|<=1 } ),

and let C_ext extend the bottom segment's upper z1 endpoint to2/5. The old sampled bases are(0,1),(1,1), and the only new sampled base q=(0,0) is an exposed vertex of their enlarged sampled hull, with a point fiber. On (1-t)C_old+tC_ext it enters already at t=1/5.

The author corrected the statement. Since the Minkowski path is contained in C_ext, every new sampled fiber is empty or its prescribed singleton whenever it appears. Old fibers remain squeezed between identical old slices of C_old and C_ext. Sampled-base exposure gives each new singleton zero measured depth. Therefore the constant-measure and constant-maximum-depth conclusion remains valid; no entry-time claim is needed.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
